description: Requirements that no recorded browser flow shows, each with the reason and the automated tests that cover it (ADR-0010). scripts/check-traceability.mjs counts an entry as covered for --strict-recordings only while some test is tagged with its id and no manifest records it.

exemptions.reason: A startup failure: with no administrator and no APP_ADMIN_INITIAL_PASSWORD the application does not start, so there is no page to record.
Startup against a database that already has the administrator: nothing visible changes, so there is nothing to record.
A late response overtaking a sign-out or expiry. Staging it means holding a response and releasing it at a chosen moment, which this suite does not do; the interceptor's own spec does.
tests: session.interceptor.spec.ts › cannot restore authentication from an in-flight response after expiry

exemptions.reason: Rounding of the opening cost to four decimals. The page shows costs to two decimals and values to the cent, and no flow here uses a quantity large enough to make the fourth decimal visible.

The server's checks of an uploaded file (extension, declared type and the file's own signature). The page applies its own checks first (FR-75, recorded); sending a file the page already refuses is an API call. The suite's requests from a page send text fields, not files.

The server's 2 MB limit. The page refuses such a file first (FR-75, recorded); the server's answer to one that gets past it is an API response. The suite's requests from a page send text fields, not files.
Spring's own 413 answer to an oversized multipart request, which needs a real HTTP exchange and a file the page would not send. The suite's requests from a page send text fields, not files.
The migration of an older database file at startup, which needs a database of the older shape and shows nothing on a page.
The opening-balance movements the migration creates for rows that existed before; the same startup path as FR-147.
Constraints of the database itself (non-negative values, unique SKU and numbers, restricted deletes), shown by direct SQL that bypasses the application on purpose.
